structure: One short ruling file, `workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-paul-2026-10-14.md`, 18 lines in the standard ruling layout: a title line ("Ruling: Paul, 14 October 2026"), a standing note that it is to confirm with Sam and was given while starting the address-book theme ahead of the team's go-ahead so its rows can build, one framing line naming what it rules on ("14 October, on inc-062 dropping County from the address book's add-details step"), the verbatim quote of the ruling itself as a single blockquote line ("Keep County."), and a "## Claims" section holding 2 numbered claims written by the main session: claim 1 the decision (the add-details step keeps a 'County (optional)' field between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code', as the edit page inc-073 and the view page inc-064 already do, replacing inc-062's criterion "The add-details step has no County field"), claim 2 its ground (the V4 Address Block on `confluence:6497338582` gives every address block the same fields, County included, and outranks the prototype, so a Design Release 2.1 page leaving County out is a prototype mistake per the EUDPA-646 ruling of 1 October 2026; and an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view and the edit form all carry would lose data on a round trip). The scope is "whole file", so nothing is left out. The verbatim quote is three words, so almost everything the file says is the main session's reading of it and must be checked back against the quote and against the framing line; the two cross-referenced documents (the V4 Confluence page, the 1 October ruling) are other sources in this programme and are not read here. The file makes one decision only, about one field on one page, so it is a single part.

parts.title: The whole ruling file
parts.scope: Every line of `sources/ruling-paul-2026-10-14.md`: the title, the to-confirm-with-Sam note, the framing line, the verbatim blockquote and both numbered claims. Nothing in the file belongs to another part, and the documents it cites (the V4 Confluence page, the 1 October ruling) are read as citations only, never opened.
covers: The verbatim quote "Keep County." read against the framing line "14 October, on inc-062 dropping County from the address book's add-details step": what the three words decide, on which page and which step

Claim 1 in full: that the address book's add-details step keeps a 'County (optional)' field, that it sits between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code', that the edit page (inc-073) and the view page (inc-064) already carry it, and that this replaces inc-062's criterion "The add-details step has no County field" — each of those four statements checked against the quote and marked verbatim or inferred accordingly, with the statement of an inferred one saying what in the quote implies it

Claim 2 in full: the V4 "Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields - V4" Address Block (`confluence:6497338582`) giving every address block the same fields including County; V4 ranking above the prototype; a Design Release 2.1 page leaving County out being a prototype mistake, citing the EUDPA-646 ruling of 1 October 2026 (`workareas/shared/catch-up-address-book-with-prototype-21/sources/ruling-paul-2026-10-01.md`); and the round-trip data-loss ground (an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view and the edit form all carry)
The optional/mandatory status asserted by the label 'County (optional)', and the field's position in the add-details step's field order

The status the file gives the ruling: to confirm with Sam, and given while starting the address-book theme ahead of the team's go-ahead so its rows can build — recorded so the reconciler knows it is unconfirmed
Which earlier report question or conflict each claim answers, named in `note` where the file says (it names inc-062's criterion as what claim 1 replaces)

A `gap` claim for anything the ruling clearly leaves open on the point it touches — for example whether the same County field is required anywhere else the prototype omits it, or what Sam's confirmation changes — and a `gap` rather than a decision for any wording the file only asks or floats
`ref` on every claim as the file and its line or list item, such as `ruling-paul-2026-10-14.md claim 2` or `ruling-paul-2026-10-14.md quote`
